summary.headline: Lumax Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore, with EBITDA margin flat at 9.2% as commodity recoveries slipped into Q2.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore and EBITDA rose 34% to INR 113 crore, with margin held at 9.2%, in line with Q1 FY26. PAT including associates rose 41.2% to INR 51 crore, at a 4.2% margin. Management said OEM price recoveries for West Asia-driven commodity and electronics costs were not realised in Q1 (about 150 bps margin drag) and are expected in Q2. FY27 capex guidance was raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore on new order wins.

financial_highlights.change: +34% y-o-y (vs INR 85 crore in Q1 FY26); margin flat y-o-y
+41.2% y-o-y (vs INR 36 crore); margin +30 bps y-o-y

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles
segments.commentary: 64% of Q1 revenue. Tata Motors Tiago headlamps and VW Taigun rear lamps launched during the quarter.

segments.name: 2 and 3-Wheelers
segments.commentary: 31% of Q1 revenue. Won Suzuki Burgman Street front turn signal orders; management said 2-Wheeler growth at HMSI is expected to be significant.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles and others
segments.commentary: 5% of Q1 revenue, unchanged y-o-y per management; won Force Motors Traveller 2 headlamp orders. The 'others' category grew 133% y-o-y, mainly Skoda/VW from Chakan 3.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: Front lighting 68% of revenue, rear lighting 23%, other products 9%.

segments.name: Customers
segments.commentary: Maruti revenue +43% y-o-y and Tata Motors +68% y-o-y, both driven by new-model SOPs. TVS also grew; Hero share declined y-o-y per analyst.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 10.5-11% maintained; Q2 margin expected to be above 10%, with Q1 recoveries expected to be realised in Q2.
FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (full year), with growth slowing in H2 on high base after GST rationalisation.
Medium term: 15-20% revenue CAGR over 3-5 years, targeting about INR 9,000 crore+ revenue by FY30-31 from INR 4,500-5,000 crore base; EBITDA of about 13% in 3-4 years.
FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore (from INR 100-150 crore); maintenance capex INR 40-50 crore. FY28 capex indicated at INR 150-200 crore, but management called it premature.
FY27 mould sales targeted at INR 250-300 crore vs INR 180-185 crore in FY26, mostly in H2 (Q3/Q4) depending on SOP timelines.
Order book about INR 2,500 crore (about 90% LED); about 60% (roughly INR 1,500 crore) to enter SOP in FY28. Maruti wallet share expected to rise from under 30% to 35-40%.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore, driven by order wins over the last four months; FY26 capex was INR 410 crore.
Bengaluru plant expansion for Maruti and Toyota models is on track, with commissioning from Q4 FY27.
Brownfield projects underway at Sanand and Bawal to support new order wins at those locations.
Localisation: SMT already 100% localised; bare PCB localisation expected to rise from 40-50% to 70-80% and connectors from about 24% to 40-50% over 2-3 years; projected gain of 70-90 bps.
demand_pricing: Industry Q1 production per SIAM: total 93.5 lakh units (+22% y-o-y); PV +17%, 2W +23%, 3W +39%, CV +15%.

Commodity recoveries: OEMs have not agreed to monthly amendments for most of the industry (only aluminium accepted); still quarterly or six-monthly. About 150 bps Q1 margin impact from unrealised recoveries.
Management expects competition intensity to rise as new players enter, but says top OEM concentration (4-5 players, 80-90% share) limits new entrants' share.
Content per vehicle for a passenger car currently INR 15,000-20,000 (outliers up to INR 30,000); management expects at least 50% growth over 4-5 years.
Honda HVAC business was about INR 18-20 crore annualised vs an estimated peak of INR 35-40 crore; Honda volumes weaker than expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin still below 10% despite LED penetration and localisation, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said OEMs have not agreed to monthly price amendments, so recoveries slipped; margin was hit about 150 bps in Q1. Realisations expected in Q2 could lift margin to about 10.5-11%, in line with FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are CV and tractor orders not yet visible, and how is the company positioned on EV content?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said CV lighting tech is standardised and the company is in talks on new platforms. Anmol Jain said CV is about 5% of revenue and grew 30-35% annualised. Lighting is powertrain-agnostic; EV content is higher in value per vehicle. 12% of order book is EV.

qa_highlights.question: Why did M&M revenue stay flat when the company holds a 40-50% wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said the XUV700 EV platform, where Lumax is not present, drove Mahindra volumes; management expects full-year growth in line with Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mould revenue outlook and FY27 capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mould sales are targeted at INR 250-300 crore (vs INR 180-185 crore), mostly in Q3/Q4. Maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crore; the rest goes to new business and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand 50-100 bps a year, and can 30% growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed about 100 bps expansion in FY27 (9.8% in FY26 to 10.5-11%). It said 30%+ quarterly growth will not persist due to high base; full-year growth guided at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the localisation plans and tooling sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said localisation is a priority but not all in-house; tooling remains imported, with tool localisation possibly by 2030. China sourcing continues for cost, with a new China office set up.

risks_watch: Q1 recoveries of about 150 bps are not yet agreed with OEMs (quarterly/six-monthly pricing still in place); Q2 margin above 10% depends on these being realised
Growth expected to slow in H2 on high base after GST rationalisation; management does not expect 30-35% quarterly growth to continue
Mould revenue (INR 250-300 crore target) is back-end loaded to Q3/Q4 and depends on SOP timelines
M&M revenue flat in Q1 despite 40-50% wallet share, as XUV700 EV platform (where Lumax is absent) drove volumes; full-year growth in line with Mahindra is expected
Competition intensity expected to rise as new players enter; Honda HVAC revenue well below estimate (INR 18-20 crore annualised vs INR 35-40 crore peak)
Only 12% of order book is EV; CV and tractor orders still not visible; FY28 capex at INR 150-200 crore called premature
Tooling remains fully imported; tool localisation possibly only by 2030; China sourcing continues for cost
key_quotes: However, that has not happened for most of the industry.
And if you look at that, then the margins would be close to about 10.5% to 11% at a total EBITDA level, which is in line with our guidance for FY 27 in the full year.
I don't think that we will continue to report a 30 - 35% each quarter.
I think it's too premature to give FY 28 capex guidance.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, order book and medium-term targets, but cautious on near-term margin, saying Q1 recoveries are still under discussion with OEMs and guidance depends on them. Evasive on CV/tractor order timing, FY28 capex and the M&M revenue shortfall, which were deflected to product mix and "premature" framing.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%), backed by a ~INR 2,500 crore order book (about 90% LED), with ~60% (~INR 1,500 crore) entering SOP in FY28, plus Bengaluru expansion commissioning from Q4 FY27 and capex raised to INR 200-250 crore on order wins; growth is expected to slow in H2 on high base, and specific capacity numbers were not given.
